learning: Iteration 4 showed mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg gave a small gain with line losses unchanged at 1.0 per run. Iteration 5 showed body_length 0.12 m lowered the score. This race tests whether a further mass reduction is the remaining yaw-inertia lever.
notes: Iteration 6 package: the Builder's mass 0.4 kg test on the iteration 4 design (best, 65.14). The controller is held exactly at iteration 4 values, so mass is the only variable changed.
rationale: Iteration 4 (mass 0.5 kg, body_length 0.16 m, y 0.05 m, 12 mm footprints, 0.06 m span, wheel_track 0.12 m, controller kp 3.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction) is the best design at 65.14. Iteration 5 showed that body_length 0.12 m lowered the score to 61.83, so the Builder correctly does not carry it forward. Mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg gave a gain of about 2 points, and iteration 3 showed the forward offset does not remove the line loss. I take the Builder's geometry exactly as proposed: mass 0.4 kg (the contract minimum), body_length 0.16 m, all other fields as in iteration 4. The controller is kept identical to iteration 4. Any gain or speed change would confound the mass test, and iteration 1 showed that raising kp and kd did not help. With no controller change, the score difference from iteration 4 can be attributed to mass alone. Expected result, as a prediction only: line losses on the s-bend and slalom fall toward 0.5 or below, max_error falls below 0.06 m, and the score rises above 65.14. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, the robot is over-turning, so mass should return to 0.5 kg.
